note: Authored names on REAL evidence shapes. Every list of window starts (seconds, 12 s windows, 9 s hop) is copied from a cached release-1 mix, as classified in docs/accuracy/release-1-miss-analysis.md; artists and titles are invented so no rule can lean on a name. The anchored_s key lists the windows whose Shazam offset anchor was reliable in the cached run (a phantom's windows mostly return several conflicting offsets and carry no anchor); an empty list is a row that fused as possible in the cached run (no usable alignment); without the key every window is anchored.

smeared_phantom.note: Section 4, the live YouTube set: a famous track 'heard' in five windows smeared over ten minutes earned a likely badge, was immune to scatter, and its hull buried two real tracks of 66 s and 72 s.

gapped_phantom.note: Section 4, the owner's 81-minute mix: the phantom is NOT scattered (132 s on air in a 282 s hull) and stays listed, but two real tracks sit in the 132 s hole between its two runs.

core_guard.note: Section 8, change 2's side effect: a CORRECT likely row whose hull (318 s) is over three times its on-air time (99 s) but which has an unbroken 57 s core. The near-miss is the same shape with two windows of the core taken out (39 s).

edge_comment.note: Section 4, contradicted: a 123 s episode, and a listener naming the NEXT track two seconds before the episode's last window ends. The next track is recognised from the following window on.

same_artist.note: Section 4, short floor: two-window rows (24 s and 21 s) by an artist with a long likely row elsewhere in the same mix; and the near-misses measured while choosing the rule.
